newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras to set aside 31 pct of budget to pay debt.
newsitem.headline: Honduras to set aside 31 pct of budget to pay debt.

text.p: The Honduran government next year will allocate 31 percent of its budget to servicing the country's $4.3 billion foreign debt, the finance minister said Wednesday.
"In the 1997 budget, 31 percent will be designated to servicing the foreign debt," Finance Minister Juan Ferrera said at a news conference.
That percentage means that $317.44 million of the proposed $1.024 billion budget would go to debt service in 1997.
The Honduran Congress is scheduled to debate the proposed budget and pass its version in December.
The proposed 1997 debt service is equal to two percent of the expected gross domestic product.
Debt service set aside in the 1996 budget represents about 35 percent of spending.
The proposed 1997 budget is much higher than the 1996 budget of $792 million.
It would allocate only $29 million to the defence ministry, compared with a $53 million request. The proposed defence spending is $2.3 million less than 1996 expenditures.
The biggest chunk of the budget, 37 percent, is set for social spending, with $157.7 million going to the education ministry, up from $125.2 million in the 1996 budget.
The communications, public works and transportation ministry would also receive a big boost to $85 million from $72.6 million in 1996.
